title: Closure calculus for sifted diagrams computing their homotopy colimits
statement:
Use the universes and infinity categories of [def-coef-complete-algebroid], the model-category terminology of [lem-coef-model-infinity-derived-adjunction], and the projective diagram model structures and coherent homotopy colimits of [lem-coef-model-colimit-localization-comparison]. Let $\mathcal M$ be a left proper combinatorial biclosed monoidal model category, not necessarily symmetric, with cofibrant tensor unit and the pushout-product axiom: the pushout product of two cofibrations is a cofibration, trivial if either factor is trivial. Biclosed means that tensoring on either side has a right adjoint, and left proper means that pushout along a cofibration preserves weak equivalences. Fix a small ordinary category $I$ such that $N(I)$ is sifted, meaning that $N(I)$-indexed colimits in spaces commute with finite products. For a strict diagram $X:I\to\mathcal M$ write $cX=\operatorname{colim}_I X$ and $hX=\operatorname{colim}_I QX$, where $QX\to X$ is a projectively cofibrant replacement. Call $X$ good if all $X(i)$ and $cX$ are cofibrant and the canonical map $hX\to cX$ is a weak equivalence. Call $f:X\to Y$ good if both endpoints are good, every $f(i)$ is a cofibration, and $cf:cX\to cY$ is a cofibration.

Constant diagrams at cofibrant objects are good. Every projectively cofibrant diagram is good, and every projective cofibration between projectively cofibrant diagrams is good. Good objects and good morphisms are closed under retracts. If $f:X\to Y$ is good and $X\to X'$ is any map with $X'$ good, then the pushout map $X'\to X'\amalg_XY$ is good. A continuous ordinal-indexed chain beginning at a good object and with good successor maps has good colimit and good maps from all its stages to that colimit; continuous means that each nonzero limit stage is the colimit of the earlier stages. If $X,Y$ are good, their pointwise tensor $X\odot Y$ is good. If $f:X\to X'$ and $g:Y\to Y'$ are good, their pointwise pushout product
$$(X'\odot Y)\amalg_{X\odot Y}(X\odot Y')\longrightarrow X'\odot Y'$$
is good. All these assertions concern the actual canonical comparison maps and ordinary cocones, with no simplicial enrichment or symmetry hypothesis.

source.place: Higher Algebra (current numbering), proof of Lemma 4.1.8.13, printed pp. 499-500, observations (1)-(7); this is Lemma 4.1.4.13 in the version cited by Haugseng Lemma 3.19. Its good-diagram calculus uses no symmetry. Online source read, not archived in literature/. No Stacks tag states this homotopy-coherent result.

proof.text: Put $\mathcal C=\mathcal M[W^{-1}]_\infty$ and write $q$ for localization. By [lem-coef-model-colimit-localization-comparison], the specified cocone from $qX$ to $q(hX)$ is colimiting. An actual map $u$ of $\mathcal M$ is a weak equivalence whenever $q(u)$ is an equivalence: the ordinary localization $\gamma$ at $W$ factors through $q$ by its universal property, so $\gamma(u)$ is an isomorphism, and [lem-coef-model-localization-detects-weak-equivalences] applies. Thus the canonical $hX\to cX$ is a weak equivalence if and only if the original cocone $qX\to q(cX)$ is colimiting. Indeed, in the forward direction, precomposition with the equivalence $q(hX)\to q(cX)$ identifies $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(q(cX),T)$ with $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(q(hX),T)$ for every $T$; composing with the colimit universal property of $q(hX)$ gives exactly the universal-property map of the original cocone. Conversely, if that original cocone is colimiting, both vertices represent the same functor $T\mapsto\lim_i\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(qX(i),T)$, and precomposition with the canonical comparison is an equivalence on all such mapping spaces. The fully faithful Yoneda criterion of [lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-presheaf-limits], applied to the opposite category, makes that comparison an equivalence. This criterion concerns the actual comparison map, not a choice of an abstract isomorphism between the vertices.

source.place: Proof of Lemma 4.1.8.13, definition of good objects, printed p. 499; universal-property criterion made explicit

proof.text: We will use elementary consequences of the lifting-class definition of cofibrations in [lem-coef-model-infinity-derived-adjunction]. A pushout of a cofibration lifts against every trivial fibration by restricting the square to the original map and extending the lift by the pushout property. A composite of cofibrations lifts by successively choosing its two lifts; a retract lifts by composing with its section and retraction. For a continuous transfinite composite of cofibrations the same lifting argument is a recursion: choose the extension at each successor and use the compatible preceding lifts at a limit. These arguments also show that all stage-to-colimit maps of such a chain are cofibrations. They apply to the initial map, so cofibrancy is preserved under these constructions starting with a cofibrant source. No assertion that arbitrary filtered colimits preserve weak equivalences is used.

source.place: Proof of Lemma 4.1.8.13, observations (1), (2), (4): lifting-class consequences written out

proof.text: For any small ordinary $J$, give $\mathcal M^J$ the projective structure of [lem-coef-model-colimit-localization-comparison]. Its colimit functor is left Quillen: its right adjoint is the constant-diagram functor, which preserves fibrations and trivial fibrations because these are objectwise. Evaluation at $j$ also preserves cofibrations. To check this directly, its right adjoint sends $T$ to the diagram $k\mapsto\prod_{\operatorname{Hom}_J(k,j)}T$; it preserves trivial fibrations since a lifting problem against a cofibration is solved in each product coordinate. Adjunction therefore converts a projective lifting problem into the required evaluation lifting problem. Consequently a projectively cofibrant diagram has cofibrant values and colimit, and a projective cofibration has cofibrant endpoint values when its endpoints are projectively cofibrant and induces a cofibration on colimits. Finally, if $D$ is projectively cofibrant, its replacement $QD\to D$ is a weak equivalence between projectively cofibrant objects. The Brown preservation clause of [lem-coef-model-infinity-derived-adjunction] for colimit makes $hD\to cD$ a weak equivalence. This proves both projective clauses of the item.

source.place: Proof of Lemma 4.1.8.13, observation (4), printed p. 500; evaluation and colimit lifting tests

proof.text: By the first, nonmonoidal assertion of [lem-coef-combinatorial-localization-presentability], $\mathcal C$ is presentable and hence cocomplete. We use the pointwise colimit theorem and the natural mapping-space universal properties of [lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-presheaf-limits]. Together with the dual cocone criterion of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus], which identifies a colimit functor as left adjoint to the constant-diagram functor on mapping spaces, they give the following interchange with its specified cocones. For small shapes $J,K$, currying identifies $\operatorname{Fun}(J,\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal C))$ with $\operatorname{Fun}(J\times K,\mathcal C)$. Each iterated colimit is left adjoint to the constant functor on $J\times K$: apply the two colimit mapping-space universal properties in succession. Reversing $J,K$ gives a left adjoint to the same constant functor, with the same component cocone. Uniqueness of a universal cocone therefore identifies the two iterated colimits and the colimit on the product. In particular $\operatorname{colim}_{N(I)}$ sends a pointwise pushout or ordinal colimit of coherent $I$-diagrams to the pushout or ordinal colimit of their colimits. This is a consequence of the stated universal properties, not an extra homotopy-colimit preservation assumption.

source.place: Observations (1), (2) of HA 4.1.8.13; formal interchange using HTT Corollary 5.1.2.3 and colimit universal properties

proof.text: By [lem-coef-sifted-nerve-index-calculus], $I$ is nonempty and connected and the constant coherent $N(I)$-diagram at any object of $\mathcal C$ has that object as colimit (the zero-variable comparison). Thus a strict constant diagram at a cofibrant $A$ has ordinary colimit $A$ and its original cocone localizes to a colimit cocone. Step 1 makes it good. For retracts, choose the functorial projective replacement allowed by the model factorizations of [lem-coef-model-infinity-derived-adjunction]. Applying this functor and ordinary colimit to a retract diagram makes its canonical $h\to c$ comparison a retract of the larger diagram's comparison. Weak equivalences are retract closed, as are cofibrations by Step 2. Objectwise and colimit cofibrancy, and the additional component and colimit cofibrations of a good morphism, consequently pass to retracts. Step 1 shows that the result also holds for any other specified cofibrant replacement.

source.place: Proof of Lemma 4.1.8.13, observation (3) and the retract argument preceding the cell induction, printed pp. 500-501

proof.text: Here is the needed pushout calculation, without simplicial enrichment. Let $A\to B$ be a cofibration between cofibrant objects, and let $A\to C$ be any map with $C$ cofibrant. Factor the latter as $A\hookrightarrow\widetilde C\xrightarrow{\sim}C$, with the second arrow a trivial fibration, using [lem-coef-model-infinity-derived-adjunction]. The span $B\leftarrow A\to\widetilde C$ is projectively cofibrant: lift first at $A$, and extend the lifts at $B$ and $\widetilde C$ using the two cofibrations. Its map to the original span is an objectwise trivial fibration, hence is a projectively cofibrant replacement in the model structure of [lem-coef-model-colimit-localization-comparison]. The map $\widetilde C\to B\amalg_A\widetilde C$ is a cofibration by Step 2. Its pushout along the weak equivalence $\widetilde C\to C$ is the map $B\amalg_A\widetilde C\to B\amalg_A C$, a weak equivalence by left properness. Therefore the original pushout cocone becomes a coherent pushout cocone by the cited homotopy-colimit comparison. Functorial factorization makes this construction natural in maps of such spans, so the pointwise theorem of Step 4 also applies to a diagram of these pushout squares.

source.place: Proof of Lemma 4.1.8.13, observation (2), printed pp. 499-500; one-cofibration homotopy-pushout calculation expanded

proof.text: Let $P=X'\amalg_XY$ as in the pushout assertion. For each $i$, Step 6 applies to $X(i)\to Y(i)$ and $X(i)\to X'(i)$: all three objects are cofibrant, and the first arrow is a cofibration. It also applies after ordinary colimit: $cX\to cY$ is a cofibration between cofibrant objects, $cX'$ is cofibrant, and $cP=cX'\amalg_{cX}cY$ by the ordinary colimit universal property. The component and colimit maps from $X'$ to $P$ are cofibrations, so their targets are cofibrant. In $\operatorname{Fun}(N(I),\mathcal C)$ the localized square is pointwise a pushout by Step 6, hence a pushout by [lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-presheaf-limits]. Step 4 commutes this pushout with $\operatorname{colim}_{N(I)}$. Since $X,Y,X'$ are good, Step 1 identifies their colimits with $q(cX),q(cY),q(cX')$ by the original cocones. The resulting pushout vertex is $q(cP)$ by the colimit version of Step 6. Its cocone is the localization of $P\to cP$, because all comparisons are induced from the same three ordinary cocones. Step 1 proves $P$ good and the two cofibration checks prove $X'\to P$ good.

source.place: Proof of Lemma 4.1.8.13, observation (2), printed p. 500

proof.text: For the ordinal assertion fix a nonempty small ordinal diagram $Z:\lambda\to\mathcal M$ starting at a cofibrant object, continuous at nonzero limits and having cofibrations at successors. It is projectively cofibrant. Indeed, to lift $Z$ against an objectwise trivial fibration, choose the lift at $0$ by cofibrancy; extend at $\beta+1$ using $Z_\beta\hookrightarrow Z_{\beta+1}$; and at a nonzero limit $\delta$ use $Z_\delta=\operatorname{colim}_{\beta<\delta}Z_\beta$ to assemble the preceding lifts. This solves precisely the projective lifting problem. Hence [lem-coef-model-colimit-localization-comparison] and Step 3 show that its ordinary colimit cocone localizes to a colimit. The same applies to every initial segment once its terms are cofibrant. All ordinals here are small in the chosen universe; enlarging universes handles any specified set-sized chain.

source.place: Proof of Lemma 4.1.8.13, observation (1), printed p. 499; ordinal projective-cofibrancy lifting recursion

proof.text:
Now take a continuous chain of diagrams starting at a good $X_0$ and with good successor maps. Transfinite induction, using Step 2 at each $i$ and after $c$, shows that every value of every limit diagram and its ordinary $I$-colimit are cofibrant, and that all stage-to-stage and stage-to-colimit maps, both componentwise and after $c$, are cofibrations. Here $c$ commutes with the ordinal colimit by its ordinary colimit universal property, so the scalar chain $cX_\beta$ is also continuous. At each limit, Step 8 says that $qX_\lambda(i)$ and $q(cX_\lambda)$ are respectively the coherent ordinal colimits of their preceding terms. The pointwise theorem of [lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-presheaf-limits] and Step 4 therefore identify
$$\operatorname{colim}_{N(I)}qX_\lambda\simeq\operatorname{colim}_{\beta<\lambda}\operatorname{colim}_{N(I)}qX_\beta\simeq\operatorname{colim}_{\beta<\lambda}q(cX_\beta)\simeq q(cX_\lambda).$$
The middle equivalence uses inductive goodness and the original cocones, so their composite is the original cocone of $X_\lambda$. Step 1 proves goodness at the limit. Successor terms are already good because their incoming successor maps are good. This induction also applies to the final colimit; if the indexing ordinal has a last stage its colimit is that stage, and the one-stage case is the identity. The cofibrations already verified give good maps from every stage to the colimit.

source.place: Proof of Lemma 4.1.8.13, observation (1), printed p. 499; continuous-chain induction including all stage maps

proof.text: Let $\mathcal M^c$ be the full subcategory of cofibrant objects. Biclosedness makes tensor preserve the initial object in each variable. Thus $(0\to A)\square(0\to D)$ identifies with $0\to A\odot D$, so the tensor of cofibrant objects is cofibrant. For cofibrant $A$, $(0\to A)\square f$ identifies with $A\odot f$; similarly $f\square(0\to A)$ identifies with $f\odot A$. The assumed pushout-product axiom makes both maps cofibrations, trivial when $f$ is trivial. Their ordinary right adjoints are supplied by biclosedness, so both partial tensor functors are left Quillen.

source.place: HA Proposition 4.1.7.2 and Example 4.1.7.6, Lemma 4.1.8.8; ordered bifunctor descent and derived partial adjunctions; pushout-product checks

proof.text: By [lem-coef-model-infinity-derived-adjunction], the two partial tensor functors of Step 10 preserve weak equivalences between cofibrant objects. A coordinatewise weak equivalence $(u,v)$ factors as $(u,1)$ followed by $(1,v)$, so tensor is relative on $\mathcal M^c\times\mathcal M^c$. Apply [lem-coef-cofibrant-inclusion-coherent-localization] to identify the localization of $N(\mathcal M^c)$ with $\mathcal C$. Finite-product preservation and the full functor-category universal property of [lem-coef-system-localization-universal] now descend $q\circ\odot$ to $B:\mathcal C\times\mathcal C\to\mathcal C$, with a coherent natural equivalence $B(qA,qD)\simeq q(A\odot D)$ on cofibrant inputs. This comparison includes diagrams and transformations because it is an equivalence in the functor category.

source.place: HA Proposition 4.1.7.2 and Example 4.1.7.6, Lemma 4.1.8.8; ordered bifunctor descent and derived partial adjunctions; relative bifunctor descent

proof.text: The bifunctor $B$ of Step 11 and its specified comparison satisfy [lem-coef-localized-bifunctor-partial-derived-adjoints], with $F=\odot$ and all three model categories equal to $\mathcal M$: Step 10 checks the two partial Quillen hypotheses. Hence $B(qA,-)$ and $B(-,qA)$ are the derived left adjoints for cofibrant $A$, and every partial functor of $B$ has a right adjoint. The first, nonmonoidal clause of [lem-coef-combinatorial-localization-presentability] makes $\mathcal C$ presentable. Apply the right-adjoint criterion of [lem-coef-presentable-infinity-adjoints] to each partial functor to conclude that $B$ preserves small colimits separately.

source.place: HA Proposition 4.1.7.2 and Example 4.1.7.6, Lemma 4.1.8.8; ordered bifunctor descent and derived partial adjunctions; derived partial adjunctions and colimit preservation

proof.text:
For good $X,Y$, their pointwise tensor has cofibrant values by Steps 10-12. Biclosedness and the ordinary finite-diagonal assertion of [lem-coef-sifted-nerve-index-calculus] identify its ordinary colimit, with its cocone, as $c(X\odot Y)\cong cX\odot cY$, which is cofibrant. Apply the coherent finite-diagonal assertion of the same node to the separately colimit-preserving bifunctor $B$ constructed in Steps 10-12:
$$\operatorname{colim}_{N(I)}q(X\odot Y)\simeq B(\operatorname{colim}_{N(I)}qX,\operatorname{colim}_{N(I)}qY)\simeq B(q(cX),q(cY))\simeq q(cX\odot cY).$$
The first comparison is the finite-diagonal colimit comparison, the second is induced by the two good cocones, and the last is tensor on cofibrant representatives. Thus their composite is exactly the localized ordinary tensor-colimit cocone, as identified above. Step 1 proves that the canonical $h(X\odot Y)\to c(X\odot Y)$ is a weak equivalence. This proves tensor-product goodness.

source.place: Proof of Lemma 4.1.8.13, observation (5), printed p. 500

proof.text: If $f:X\to X'$ is good and $Y$ is good, Step 13 gives good endpoints for both $f\odot\mathrm{id}_Y$ and $\mathrm{id}_Y\odot f$. Their components are cofibrations because each $Y(i)$ is cofibrant and tensor on that side is left Quillen, as shown in Steps 10-12. Their colimit maps identify, by the natural ordinary comparison in [lem-coef-sifted-nerve-index-calculus], with $cf\odot\mathrm{id}_{cY}$ and $\mathrm{id}_{cY}\odot cf$. These are cofibrations by cofibrancy of $cY$ and the same pushout-product calculation. Both ordered tensor morphisms are therefore good.

source.place: Proof of Lemma 4.1.8.13, observation (6), printed p. 500; both ordered variants

proof.text: Finally let $f:X\to X'$ and $g:Y\to Y'$ be good and put $P=(X'\odot Y)\amalg_{X\odot Y}(X\odot Y')$. Both maps out of $X\odot Y$ are good by Step 14, so Step 7 makes $P$ good. Its target $X'\odot Y'$ is good by Step 13. At every $i$ the displayed arrow $P(i)\to X'(i)\odot Y'(i)$ is $f(i)\square g(i)$, a cofibration by the assumed pushout-product axiom. Ordinary colimit preserves the pushout, and the natural ordinary tensor comparisons of [lem-coef-sifted-nerve-index-calculus] identify its colimit arrow with $(cf)\square(cg)$, again a cofibration. These are precisely the remaining two conditions for this arrow to be good. Throughout the proof the identifications are induced by the original cocones and the functorial replacement maps, which establishes the final canonical-map assertion of the item.

source.place: Proof of Lemma 4.1.8.13, observation (7), printed p. 500

lean.statement: theorem siftedGoodDiagramCalculus {M : Type u} [Category.{v} M] [ModelCategory M] [HasLimits M] [HasColimits M] [MonoidalCategory M] [MonoidalClosed M] (hRightClosed : ∀ A : M, (tensorRight A).IsLeftAdjoint) (hM : CombinatorialModelCategory.{u, v, w} M) (hUnit : IsCofibrant (𝟙_ M)) (hLeftProper : (weakEquivalences M).IsStableUnderCobaseChangeAgainst (cofibrations M)) (hPushoutProduct : PushoutProductAxiom M) : ∀ (I : Type v) [SmallCategory I], SSet.Enhanced.IsInfinitySifted (nerve I) → (∀ (A : M), IsCofibrant A → GoodDiagram ((Functor.const I).obj A)) ∧ (∀ (X : I ⥤ M), ProjectivelyCofibrant X → GoodDiagram X) ∧ (∀ {X Y : I ⥤ M} (f : X ⟶ Y), ProjectivelyCofibrant X → ProjectivelyCofibrant Y → ProjectiveCofibration f → GoodMorphism f) ∧ (∀ {X Y : I ⥤ M}, Retract X Y → GoodDiagram Y → GoodDiagram X) ∧ (∀ {X Y X' Y' : I ⥤ M} (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : X' ⟶ Y'), RetractArrow f g → GoodMorphism g → GoodMorphism f) ∧ (∀ {X Y X' : I ⥤ M} (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : X ⟶ X'), GoodMorphism f → GoodDiagram X' → GoodMorphism (pushout.inr f g)) ∧ (∀ (J : Type v) [LinearOrder J] [OrderBot J] [SuccOrder J] [WellFoundedLT J] (F : J ⥤ (I ⥤ M)) [F.IsWellOrderContinuous], GoodDiagram (F.obj ⊥) → (∀ j : J, ¬ IsMax j → GoodMorphism (F.map (homOfLE (Order.le_succ j)))) → ∀ (c : Cocone F), IsColimit c → GoodDiagram c.pt ∧ ∀ j : J, GoodMorphism (c.ι.app j)) ∧ (∀ {X Y : I ⥤ M}, GoodDiagram X → GoodDiagram Y → GoodDiagram (X ⊗ Y)) ∧ (∀ {X X' Y Y' : I ⥤ M} (f : X ⟶ X') (g : Y ⟶ Y'), GoodMorphism f → GoodMorphism g → GoodMorphism (Arrow.mk f □ Arrow.mk g).hom)
